original_card.question: Can a decoder deliver the local paid mass in fewer, larger-rank children (block frame climbs instead of rank-1 to rank-3 steps)?
methods: Find one exact small decoding identity whose frame path climbs in blocks, and price its complete per-call profile.
Bound the best effective child rank achievable for one fixed support alphabet, including copies, frames and restoration.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A per-call local profile, with all copied information, frames and restoration counted, whose ceiling exceeds the selected word's by at least 5%; masked or overcomplete supports must change an assumption of the eight-term all-pairs bound.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin. Ideal budget: rank-16 delivery is 2.31x (levers.py).
original_card.bottleneck_link: Rank-1 children are about half of recursive cost; the selected word's effective child rank is about 3.9. Larger-rank delivery lowers recursive cost per unit of paid mass.
allowed_variations: One masked, overcomplete or block decoder family with exact labels and supports.
A scoped lower bound on effective rank for one alphabet.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Repacking idle remainders of an unchanged word (covered by the packing ceiling).
Repeating the eight-term all-pairs search inside its proved scope.

scope_change_reason: I tested one correlated gauge family on the merged coordinate-frame-plus-root nine-normal decoder. Its P112 puncture and one-dimensional coefficient dependency differ from the symmetric ten-term Householder witness, A8 simplex punctures and rank-16 diagonal batches. The full ternary global-shift box is an exact, finite construction screen rather than a repeat of the predecessor's independent per-root ratio-class census.
actual_scope: For the E8 P112 puncture obtained by deleting the eight coordinate-frame lines, use the nine normals consisting of those eight coordinate roots and the first extra root with four nonzero coordinate-frame inner products. For every global integer shift w in {-1,0,1}^8, add <r_i,w> times the exact null dependency to every root's base coefficient row. Enumerate the exact F2 copied-information cost and test whether all nine terms can be active below cost 64.
bottleneck_link: A lower sum of F2 pairing ranks is a necessary local copied-information saving before frame, hosting and restoration charges. The known P112 comparator is 64; this family has no active nine-term member below 72, so the proposed active overcomplete decoder has no local cost headroom to price into the selected recursive profile.
stop_rule: Exhaust exactly all 3^8 global shifts, compute every term's rational support and F2 pairing rank, and verify the best active decoder on all 112^2 live pairs. Stop after the full census; do not infer a bound for arbitrary per-root shifts, other frames, other punctures or shifts outside the ternary box.
evidence: The exact census has 6,561 shifts: 2 produce cost 64 with one inactive term, 3 active nine-term decoders cost 72 (all nine ranks equal 8), and the remaining 6,556 active decoders cost 73. The best active cost is 72. All three best active identities pass on 12,544 live pairs each; a one-coefficient mutation is rejected. No kappa, full circuit, frame invoice or selected-record change is claimed.
author: Cinna Davis
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in scope selection, exact search, verification and prose. No independent human review or proof-assistant formalization is claimed.

open_questions.question: Does a larger bounded global-shift box contain a lower-copy all-active decoder on this same puncture, or do useful zero patterns require independently chosen per-root gauges?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This determines whether correlated gauges can improve the P112 copy invoice before any frame or recursive expenses are paid.
open_questions.first_step: Select a fresh scoped assignment and derive an optimistic cost threshold before enumerating a new shift domain; reuse the exact integer support-mask calculation but pin a new explicit box.
open_questions.blocked_by: The present result exhausts only the ternary global-shift box, and the known broader per-root ratio-class family is predecessor work rather than evidence for a larger correlated box.
